newsitem.title: FRANCE: French Communists want rethink on stability pact.
newsitem.headline: French Communists want rethink on stability pact.

text.p: French Communist party leader Robert Hue called on Monday for changes in the thinking surrounding a pact designed to enforce budgetary stability after the launch of a single currency.
"The conception that until now has prevailed concerning this stability pact should be modified significantly," Hue told Europe 1 radio.

"The idea of a re-orientation of European policy, present in the speeches of (French Prime Minister) Lionel Jospin, should be reflected by arranging this pact in such a way that it does not injure national sovereignty," Hue told Europe 1 radio.
Hue, whose party holds the balance of power after last week's Socialist election victory, stopped short of calling for Jospin's government to renegotiate or dump the pact reached in Dublin last year.
Jospin and his Socialist-led government have reaffirmed France's commitment to launching the euro currency on time, but have not yet stated a definitive position on the stability pact.
That was expected to be disclosed at a meeting of European Union finance ministers in Luxembourg on Monday.
Jospin has said that all parties in the broad-left government, which includes two full Communist ministers, will have to adhere to the Socialist line on Europe.
